name: Question 15
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-8)\,i-4t\,j$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-8)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i-4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ [({t}^{2}-8)\,i-4t\,j]\cdot (2t\,i-4\,j) & =0 \\ ({t}^{2}-8)\cdot 2t+(-4t)\cdot (-4) & =0 \\ 2{t}^{3}-16t+16t & =0 \\ 2{t}^{3} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only solution is $t=0.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)=({0}^{2}-8)\,i-4(0)\,j=-8i,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(-8,0).$

Question 15
?

Given the curve r(t)=(t2−8)i−4tj, find all of the points at which r′(t) and r(t) are perpendicular.

a
 (−8,0) and (−7,−4)
b
 (9,12)
c
 (−4,8) and (9,12)
d
 (−7,−4) and (−4,−8)
e
(−8,0)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t): r′(t)=ddt(t2−8)i+ddt(−4t)j=2ti−4j

The vectors r(t) and r′(t) are perpendicular for some value of the parameter t if and only if r(t)⋅r′(t)=0. So, we have

r(t)⋅r′(t)=0[(t2−8)i−4tj]⋅(2ti−4j)=0(t2−8)⋅2t+(−4t)⋅(−4)=02t3−16t+16t=02t3=0.

Therefore, the only solution is t=0.

Finally, since

r(0)=(02−8)i−4(0)j=−8i,

we conclude that r(t) and r′(t) are perpendicular at the point (−8,0).
